idea: 026 Rate shock, then rotation: Dow against Nasdaq after a large 5-day move in the 10-year yield
hypothesis: A large 5-day rise (fall) of the US 10-year Treasury yield, scaled by its own past volatility, is followed over the next two trading days by the Dow outperforming (underperforming) the Nasdaq 100.
mechanism: Nasdaq shares carry distant cash flows (long duration) and react more to yields than the Dow; slow money (pension rebalancing, style funds) rotates over several days after a rate shock. Information from the bond market, not from index charts; market-neutral hedged pair. Not a closed family: not intraday index opening rules, not a lead-lag between markets' prices (signal is a rate level change, traded days later), not macro event days. Practitioner evidence only; prior very low to low; the sign may differ across 2013-2019 and 2020-2021.

data.signal: FRED DGS10 (10-year constant-maturity Treasury yield, daily, percent), fredgraph.csv via kit.data.fred from 2011-01-01 (warm-up), cut 2021-12-31. KNOWN-AT rule: observation date D + 1 business day 13:00 UTC (data.rule_next_bday_utc(13, 1)); the Treasury posts D's curve on D 15:30-18:00 New York, so a live robot reading treasury.gov has it before 08:00 NY on D+1.
data.publication_lag: min lag 1 business day + 13 h (rule above); DGS10 is a market series, not revised (sources.md section 1).
data.prices: kit.data.load_bars('us30'), load_bars('us100'): prepared H1 BID bars (~/explore_data/h1, aggregated from the lab's one-minute bars); us30 starts 2013-09-30. Pair = sim.pair_book('us30/us100', 'us30', 'us100', kind='ratio'): long pair = long us30 and short us100, equal notional; both swap triple Friday.
data.in_sample_years: 2013-10 .. 2021 (8.25 years); power check from DGS10 alone: 2,063 observation days from 2013-10-01, 605 with |z| >= 1 (250 with |z| >= 1.5); with one position at a time and a 2-trading-day hold about 393 signals can be taken (196 up, 197 down) >= 250.

rule_main.signal: y_D = DGS10 on observation day D (FRED rows, missing days dropped). d_D = y_D - y of the 5th previous observation (5 trading days). s_D = sample sd of d over the 250 observations BEFORE D (d shifted by one, rolling 250, past only). z_D = d_D / s_D. Known at D + 1 business day 13:00 UTC.
rule_main.side: z_D >= +1: +1 (long us30, short us100); z_D <= -1: -1 (short us30, long us100); else no signal.
rule_main.entry: known_at = 10:00 New York (DST-correct) of the next business day (Mon-Fri) after D, which is always after the 13:00 UTC known-at time; entry at the open of the first pair H1 bar opening at or after known_at, max_wait_h = 1 (signal dropped if no pair bar by 11:00 NY, e.g. a US holiday).
rule_main.overlap: one position at a time on the pair (kit.sim mode 'one'); every-signal variant for the every-signal bar

changes_vs_scout: Scout: entry 09:30 NY on D+1, exit 16:00 NY on D+3. With hourly bars aligned on the UTC hour, 09:30 NY is mid-bar: the nearest computable entry without anticipation is the 10:00 NY bar open. The kit's clock exit takes the next HH:MM after entry (same day) and an event exit cannot tie an exit to each trade's own day, so the exit is ('bdays', 2) from entry = 10:00 NY on D+3 (6 h earlier than the scout's 16:00; the nearest computable). Everything else (z definition, thresholds, no overlap, stop 1.5 x D20 of the spread) as the scout wrote it.
configuration_notes: Neighbours fixed before any result: z threshold 0.75 / 1.25 / 1.5; hold 1 or 3 business days; stop 1.0 or 2.0 x D20; yield change over 3 or 10 trading days (sd window 250 of the same change). Every configuration on the same pair, entry 10:00 NY next business day.
costs: kit.costs (lab/r2/fp_costs.json, FP Raw), each leg its own costs: gross, net, spread and slippage x1.5
bars: CHARTER.md 'The bars' for one market (the pair is ONE market, lead's ruling (a)) on 01_main, computed by kit.judge.verdict; random-entry null 2000 draws with the main's exit and stop; weekly corr with the ten <= 0.30; deflated Sharpe on N_all (N_main reported)
split: IS only (to 2021-12-31). No VAL look in this run (lead's instruction); an attack (attack.py) only if every IS bar passes.
